text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Democratic Rally leader Yiannakis Matsis, who suffered a heart attack earlier this week, is out of danger.
- Nurses threaten to step up their strike measures at state-run hospitals.
- Irish presidency representative in Cyprus for contacts on how the EU can help towards a solution of the Cyprus problem.
- Former chairman of the state-run electricity authority defends controversial tenders for the Vassiliko power station.
- Politicians in the opposition camp are being trailed by detectives, says communist Akel MP.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash threatens an imminent flare-up of hostilities in Cyprus while the United Nations still pursue unmanning of ceasefire line positions.
- It is not what you know but who you know to get a position in the civil service, says a pressure group.
- Women from eastern Europe arrive in Cyprus as tourists but end up working in cabarets or bars.
